To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the power control scheme is effective to reduce interference, the contention control scheme is effective when the transmission range of a CR node is large and the hidden primary receiver is a major cause of interference.
the interference experienced at a primary receiver can be reduced by power control, by contention control, or by hybrid power/contention controls.
power and contention controls can effectively reduce interference in cognitive radio networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the aggregate interference modeling for CR networks with various interference management mechanisms.
interference modeling of CR networks with power control, contention management and hybrid power/contention controls.
the interference modeling of CR networks employing various interference mitigation techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interference of a CR network is a function of the transmission power, the contention probability of the CR node and the number of CR nodes in a CR network.

the proposed power control scheme is more effective in interference reduction than the contention control scheme, but the latter is much easier to implement and has less complexity in computation and implementation.
the proposed interference model is accurate and effective in modeling the interference of CR network with different interference control schemes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed interference models for the three cases of power, contention and hybrid controls are useful for the performance analysis of the primary network and for the secondary network in a CR system.
, in this paper, we have proposed a novel interference modeling approach for cognitive radio networks employing power and/or contention controls.

the power control and the contention control can be adopted to govern the interference caused by a CR network, and the hybrid power and contention control can be more effective in terms of interference reduction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aggregate interference from CR networks can be modeled as log-normal random variables.
the interference experienced by primary receivers is not a random variable but a function of time, which can be accurately estimated by our models.
the interference received at the receiver of a primary network can be accurately characterized by a simple log-normal distribution, which is a good approximation to the true distribution.
